confirmed.title: After the merge, the checker 'confirms' #18's eaves rows' 'To comply: move the building X farther from that lot line', but it only tests the one eaves measure. Following the advice can still leave the row failing
confirmed.detail: #18's eaves rows are named 'Eaves into side yard' etc., so `_hint` treats them as yards (`name.split(",")[0].endswith("yard")`) and writes 'To comply: move the building {gap} farther from that lot line.' Their measures (side_yard_smaller_eaves …) are not in YARD_MEASURES, so `_drawn_advice` does not use arch's `_yard_advice`. It falls through to `{"ways": [{"text": ..., "changes": {m: change}}]}`. arch's confirm_advice then checks that advice by changing ONLY that one measure. Its docstring says: 'Pieces only ever change one measurement, one wall pulled back, so the re-decision is exact.' The words, though, say to move the whole building, and that also cuts the opposite side's eaves distance. Arch's round 4/5 fixes removed exactly this kind of whole-building move advice from the yard rows; the eaves rows from the other side of the merge bypass that fix. Reproduced on test_every_reading's 60 ft lot with floors(4,30,51,70,2): 'Eaves into side yard' fails at 4'-0" (needs 8'-0") and shows the kept hint 'To comply: move the building 4'-0" farther from that lot line.' Doing exactly that (floors(8,30,55,70,2)) still gives does_not_comply at 5'-0" with a new hint, 'move the building 3'-0"'. The advice loops, and no move can work (47 ft of house on a 60 ft lot). The row's verdict is not a false pass, but the panel presents a 'To comply' as checker-confirmed when following it does not comply. That breaks arch's stated guarantee that every To comply is the checker's to confirm. It also names no line ('that lot line'). test_doing_what_to_comply_says_makes_that_row_comply… skips these rows ('name in pull or name == "Building height"'), which is why the suite stays green.
confirmed.evidence: present.py _hint: `if name.split(",")[0].endswith("yard"):  return f"To comply: move the building {gap} farther from that lot line."`; _drawn_advice: `if m in YARD_MEASURES ...: return _yard_advice(...)` / `return {"head": "To comply", "ways": [{"text": hint[len("To comply: "):-1], "changes": {m: change}}]}`; YARD_MEASURES = ("front_yard", "side_yard_smaller", "side_yard_larger", "rear_yard"); check.confirm_advice: `after = statuses(part["changes"])` with `_changed(measured, changes)` touching only the named measure. Run output: `4 Eaves into side yard does_not_comply 4'-0" 8'-0" | To comply: move the building 4'-0" farther from that lot line.` then `8 Eaves into side yard does_not_comply 5'-0" 8'-0" | To comply: move the building 3'-0" farther from that lot line.`
confirmed.pin: New test in packages/design_checker/tests/test_moved_and_crossing.py (or test_present.py): run(floors(4,30,51,70,2)) on test_every_reading's LOT. For each 'Eaves into …' row whose hint starts with 'To comply', do what the hint says and assert that row's status is COMPLIES and no other row got worse. Alternatively, extend the `pull` map in test_doing_what_to_comply_says_makes_that_row_comply_on_the_tax_map_and_on_a_survey to the eaves rows. Today: hint kept, followed, still does_not_comply.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Give the eaves measures the same advice shape as the yards: map each *_eaves measure to its yard line in `_yard_line`/`_drawn_advice`/`comply_hint`, and phrase it as the requirement for every part, eaves included ('keep every part of the building, eaves included, at least 8'-0" from the west side lot line — now 4'-0" at its closest'). That is the one-measure change confirm_advice actually simulates. Stop `_hint` from saying 'move the building' for any row the checker confirms by changing one measure.

confirmed.title: 'To comply: move it back onto the lot.' is kept unconfirmed on yard rows, where moving back onto the lot is not enough to comply
confirmed.detail: The merge marks the crossing advice `"crossing": True`, so settle passes it through unchanged and confirm_advice `continue`s past it without checking it. Every other 'To comply' in the merged code must make its row comply when followed (arch's round-4 rule). On a yard row the crossing advice claims compliance it does not give: the side yard is 0'-0" against 10'-0". Reproduced with floors(50,30,65,70,2) on the 60 ft lot: 'Side yard, narrower' and 'Eaves into side yard' do_not_comply, both with hint 'To comply: move it back onto the lot.' Doing exactly that (floors(45,30,60,70,2), now on the lot) still gives does_not_comply 0'-0" vs 10'-0" and 0'-0" vs 8'-0". Only then does the row show its real advice: 'keep every part … at least 10'-0"'. The architect is told a step is enough to comply when it is not. The new test test_a_crossing_building_is_told_only_to_move_back_onto_the_lot_and_the_checker_keeps_it pins this wording as correct.
confirmed.evidence: present.py: `if row.get("Crossing"): st, why = FAILS, ...; advice = {"head": "To comply", "ways": [{"text": "move it back onto the lot", "changes": {}}], "crossing": True}`; settle: `if (i.get("_advice") or {}).get("crossing"): pass`; check.confirm_advice: `if advice.get("crossing"): continue`. Run: `50 Side yard, narrower does_not_comply 0'-0" 10'-0" | To comply: move it back onto the lot.` → `45 Side yard, narrower does_not_comply 0'-0" 10'-0" | To comply: keep every part of the building at least 10'-0" from that side lot line …`
confirmed.pin: Change test_a_crossing_building_is_told_only_to_move_back_onto_the_lot_and_the_checker_keeps_it (packages/design_checker/tests/test_moved_and_crossing.py) so it asserts that a crossing yard row's hint either does not start with 'To comply' or names the yard's requirement (e.g. contains "10'-0\""). As written, it asserts the bare 'To comply: move it back onto the lot.' that fails when followed.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not head the crossing step 'To comply' unless it is sufficient. Where the row has a yard requirement, combine the move-back with that requirement ('move it back onto the lot and keep every part at least 10'-0" from the east side lot line'). Otherwise use a non-'To comply' head ('First: move it back onto the lot'). Keep confirm_advice's skip only for rows whose failing fact is the crossing itself (proposed 'partly off the lot', not YARD_ROWS).

I could not refute this. I read the code and ran the case myself.

**What the code does**
- present.py:1148-1158: when a row has `row["Crossing"]` set, the code fails the row and gives it one fixed piece of advice, `{"head": "To comply", "ways": [{"text": "move it back onto the lot", "changes": {}}], "crossing": True}`. Yard rows are included. The guard at line 1157 (`node.left.id not in YARD_ROWS`) only changes the proposed/required text. It does not change the advice.
- present.py:842: `settle` sees the `crossing` flag and does nothing (`pass`). So `comply_hint` never produces the yard's own figure for these rows.
- check.py:469-470: `confirm_advice` sees `advice.get("crossing")` and skips the row (`continue`), so the `holds()` check (lines 473-480) never runs. For every other "To comply", `holds()` requires that following the advice makes the row comply. Any way that fails that check is dropped. The crossing advice is the only one exempt from it.

**What I ran**
I ran this with the repo's `.venv` and the test helpers `floors`/`run`/`rows` from test_every_reading.py.

With `floors(50,30,65,70,2)` (the building crosses the side lot line):
- 'Side yard, narrower': does not comply, 0'-0" against 10'-0". Hint: "To comply: move it back onto the lot."
- 'Eaves into side yard': does not comply, 0'-0" against 8'-0". Same hint.

I then followed that advice exactly with `floors(45,30,60,70,2)`, which puts the building back on the lot:
- 'Side yard, narrower': still does not comply, 0'-0" against 10'-0". Only now does it show the real advice: "keep every part … at least 10'-0"".
- 'Eaves into side yard': still does not comply, 0'-0" against 8'-0".

So on yard rows, the advice tells the architect one step is enough to comply when it is not. That breaks the guarantee `confirm_advice` enforces for every other piece of advice.

**Why it is not a deliberate, consistent pattern**
The new test `test_a_crossing_building_is_told_only_to_move_back_onto_the_lot_and_the_checker_keeps_it` (tests/test_moved_and_crossing.py:73) does lock in this wording. But that is the very behaviour being questioned. Every other "To comply" path goes through the `holds()` check, so the crossing advice is the one exception, not a pattern used elsewhere.

**New or pre-existing**
This is new on this branch. The crossing advice and both bypasses are marked PR 18 in the code comments.
